reason: A page without remaining vertical scroll must pass the wheel to its transcript even when page overscroll chaining is disabled.
Upward wheel input inside a frame must release the transcript's automatic following.
Subsequent content updates must preserve the position chosen by an upward gesture.
Boundary wheel forwarding must work in both directions.
Forwarding cancels the original default action so native cross-frame chaining cannot apply the same delta twice.
A scrollable page control consumes input while it has room in the requested direction.
A nested control at its upper edge must allow the reader to continue upward into the conversation.
Predominantly horizontal trackpad gestures remain inside a horizontal page control.
Small horizontal trackpad drift must not trap an upward reading gesture at a vertical boundary.
A page taller than the frame height cap retains its own scrolling.
A height-capped page at its upper edge forwards upward input to its transcript.
A wide preview scrolls its own page while the conversation stays in place.
The wide preview must keep background scrolling blocked at its own page boundary.
Closing the preview restores ordinary inline wheel forwarding on the same frame.
